title: IS12:: arrayio.c (119.1)

lines.explanation: This is a preprocessor command. System header file stdio.h will be   inserted there during compilation.  We include stdio.h header file because it contains function prototypes for printf

The define statement sets up a meaningful, symbolic constant for the size (dimemsion) of the array that is used consistently throughout the program.  In this case, wherever N is used, the value 7 will replace it literally.   Defining constants is useful i

lines.code: int ar[DIM]; /* elements from ar[0] to ar[DIM-1]; */
lines.explanation: An array of 5 integer values is defined.  Elements of this array have indexes from 0 to 4.
i is the loop control (counter) variable that keeps track of loop iterations.
We have to start with array element with index 0. So we assign i to 0

Last iteration of this loop happens with when i has value DIM - 1 - i.e., for the last element of the array. On the next step, i will get value DIM (5 in this case) and since 5 < 5 is false (0), the loop will end. This the loop will execute exactly once f
This prints a prompt for entering the value for the next element of the array
This line shows that a value can be "scanned" inside an element of an array the same way as we can scan in into a regular variable.
Loop counter is incremented before the beginning of the next iteration

lines.code: printf("This is what you have entered:\n");

lines.explanation: Last iteration of this loop happens with when i has value DIM - 1 - i.e., for the last element of the array. On the next step, i will get value DIM (7 in this case) and since 7 < 7 is false (0), the loop will end. This the loop will execute exactly once f
This line prints the value of array element with index i. Since i will take different values at different iterations of this loop running from 0 to 6, all values will be printed one by one
This statement prints one single line
